name: Ferrum-Glacies
description: Ferrum-Glacies is a frozen world with a heart of iron: its crust is thin for an ice planet, and the magnetic field that pours from its metallic core drags auroras across the sky in permanent green ribbons. Glaciers flow between ranges of iron-stained rock, pooling in methane lakes frozen mid-ripple, and at the southern pole a meteor crater thirty kilometers wide holds ice so old it flows like slow glass.

The cold here is architectural—it builds pressure in your boots, stiffens seals, makes sound brittle. Wind off the glaciers carries a faint metallic taste, and the auroras hiss at the edge of hearing on bad nights. In the crystal caverns beneath the crust, silence is total except for the tick of ice adjusting to the dark.

Half-buried in the crater's rim lies the colony ship Meridian's Promise, down intact enough that her hull numbers still read; she vanished with nine thousand souls two centuries ago, and her logs end forty minutes before landing. The ice around her is stained rust-red in a ring no contamination protocol explains. Core samples from beneath the wreck have recovered fossil microbes—native life, extinct eons before any ship fell—arranged in the sediment in patterns too regular to be natural.

Platinum lodes vein the crater floor below the ice, close enough to the wreck that every mining survey becomes an archaeology dig, which the charter forbids. The descendants' guilds hold a legal injunction against disturbing the site, but the claim auction proceeds anyway—and someone has already cut a fresh tunnel toward the hull.
